translations.literal: Shi Jianu; son: Li Manzhu; Li Manzhu's grandson: Wanzhetu; Mengge Buhua; son: Samanhashili.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu — Li Manzhu (son) — Wanzhetu (Li Manzhu's grandson) — Mengge Buhua — Samanhashili (son).

translations.literal: Mengge Timur; Mengge Timur's younger brother: Fancha; son: Dongshan; Dongshan's son: Tuoluo; Tuoluo's son: Tuoyuanbao; Fancha's son: Buhuatou.
translations.idiomatic: Mengge Timur — Fancha (younger brother) — Dongshan (son) — Tuoluo (Dongshan's son) — Tuoyuanbao (Tuoluo's son) — Buhuatou (Fancha's son).

sentences.zh: 王杲王兀堂}}

translations.literal: Wang Gao; Wang Wutang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao; Wang Wutang.

sentences.zh: 阿哈出，遼東邊外女眞頭人。

translations.literal: A Ha Chu was a Jurchen tribal headman beyond the eastern border of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: A Ha Chu was a Jurchen chieftain living beyond Liaodong's eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 太祖以建州衞起兵。

translations.literal: The Taizu raised troops from the Jianzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor rose in arms through the Jianzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 建州設衞，始永樂元年十一月辛丑，初爲指揮使者，阿哈出也，明賜姓名李誠善，所屬授千百戶、鎭撫，賜誥印、冠服、鈔幣有差。

translations.literal: The Jianzhou Guard was established, beginning on xinchou day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yongle; the first commander was A Ha Chu; the Ming bestowed the surname and personal name Li Chengshan; his subordinates were appointed centurions and millenarians and garrison commissioners, and patents of appointment, seals, caps and robes, and paper money were granted in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou was made a guard in the eleventh month of Yongle 1 (1403); its first commander was A Ha Chu, whom the Ming ennobled as Li Chengshan. His followers received ranks as centurions, millenarians, and garrison commissioners, along with graded gifts of patents, seals, court dress, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，阿哈出朝於明。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, A Ha Chu presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle 3, A Ha Chu came to court.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，忽的河、法胡河、卓兒河、海剌河諸女眞頭人哈喇等朝於明，以其地屬建州衞，哈喇等授千百戶。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, the Jurchen headmen Hala and others of the Hudie River, Fahu River, Zhuo'er River, and Haila River presented themselves at the Ming court; their territories were placed under the Jianzhou Guard, and Hala and the others were appointed centurions and millenarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongle 6, Jurchen leaders along the Hudie, Fahu, Zhuo'er, and Haila rivers—including Hala—paid court to the Ming. Their lands were annexed to Jianzhou, and they were given centurion and millenarian commissions.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，阿哈出朝於明。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year, A Ha Chu presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yongle 7, A Ha Chu again came to court.

sentences.zh: 阿哈出子二：釋加奴、猛哥不花。

translations.literal: A Ha Chu had two sons: Shi Jianu and Mengge Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: A Ha Chu had two sons, Shi Jianu and Mengge Buhua.

sentences.zh: 八年，成祖親征出塞，釋加奴率所屬從戰有功。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Yongle Emperor personally campaigned beyond the passes, Shi Jianu led his followers to join the campaign and performed meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 8 the Yongle Emperor led a personal campaign beyond the frontier; Shi Jianu brought his men and distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 八月乙卯，以釋加奴爲都指揮僉事，賜姓名李顯忠，所屬昝卜賜姓名張志義，阿剌失賜姓名李從善，可捏賜姓名郭以誠，皆爲正千戶。

translations.literal: On yimao day of the eighth month, Shi Jianu was made assistant regional commander; he was granted the surname and personal name Li Xianzhong; his subordinates Zanbu were granted the surname and personal name Zhang Zhiyi, Alashi Li Congshan, and Kenie Guo Yicheng—all as senior centurions.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the eighth month Shi Jianu was promoted to assistant regional commander and given the Chinese name Li Xianzhong. His followers Zanbu, Alashi, and Kenie received the names Zhang Zhiyi, Li Congshan, and Guo Yicheng and were all appointed senior centurions.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，釋加奴舉猛哥不花爲毛憐衛指揮使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year, Shi Jianu recommended Mengge Buhua as commander of the Maolian Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongle 9, Shi Jianu nominated his brother Mengge Buhua to command the Maolian Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，永樂三年設毛憐衞，以頭人巴兒遜爲指揮使；

translations.literal: At first, in the third year of Yongle the Maolian Guard was established, with the headman Ba'ersun as commander;
translations.idiomatic: The Maolian Guard had been founded in Yongle 3, with the chieftain Ba'ersun as its first commander;

sentences.zh: 至是從釋加奴請，以命其弟。

translations.literal: at this time, following Shi Jianu's request, the post was given to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: but now, at Shi Jianu's request, the command was transferred to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 十年，釋加奴等歲祲乏食，遼東都指揮巫凱以聞，成祖命發粟賑之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Shi Jianu and others suffered famine and lacked food; the regional commander of Liaodong, Wu Kai, reported it, and the Yongle Emperor ordered grain distributed in relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 10 famine left Shi Jianu and his people short of food. Liaodong commander Wu Kai reported the distress, and the Yongle Emperor ordered grain relief.

sentences.zh: 猛哥帖木兒者，亦女眞頭人，其弟曰凡察，與阿哈出父子並起，明析置建州左衞處之，以爲指揮使。

translations.literal: Mengge Timur was also a Jurchen headman; his younger brother was called Fancha; he rose together with A Ha Chu and his sons; the Ming separately established the Left Jianzhou Guard to settle them and made him commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mengge Timur was another Jurchen chieftain; his younger brother was Fancha. Rising alongside A Ha Chu's line, they were given their own Left Jianzhou Guard, with Mengge Timur as commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年十月，與釋加奴、猛哥不花同朝於明。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eleventh year, he presented himself at the Ming court together with Shi Jianu and Mengge Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle 11 he came to court with Shi Jianu and Mengge Buhua.

sentences.zh: 十四年，釋加奴、猛哥不花朝於明，爲所屬乞官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Shi Jianu and Mengge Buhua presented themselves at the Ming court and requested offices for their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 14, Shi Jianu and Mengge Buhua came to court to seek commissions for their followers.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，猛哥不花朝於明。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, Mengge Buhua presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongle 15, Mengge Buhua came to court.

sentences.zh: 十二月，釋加奴上言：「顏春頭人月兒速哥率其孥來歸，請屬於建州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Shi Jianu submitted a memorial: "The Yanchun headman Yue'ersuge has led his household to submit; I request they be placed under Jianzhou."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shi Jianu memorialized: "The Yanchun chieftain Yue'ersuge has brought his family to submit; please attach them to Jianzhou."

sentences.zh: 」釋加奴、猛哥不花、猛哥帖木兒屢爲所屬乞官。

translations.literal: " Shi Jianu, Mengge Buhua, and Mengge Timur repeatedly requested offices for their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu, Mengge Buhua, and Mengge Timur kept petitioning for offices for their men.

sentences.zh: 十八年閏正月，成祖命無功不得乞官，賜敕戒諭之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the eighteenth year, the Yongle Emperor ordered that without merit one might not request offices, and granted an edict admonishing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of Yongle 18 the Yongle Emperor ruled that offices could not be sought without merit, and sent an edict of warning.

sentences.zh: 十九年十月，猛哥不花朝於明。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year, Mengge Buhua presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle 19, Mengge Buhua came to court.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月，成祖親征出塞，猛哥不花率子弟及所屬從，賜弓矢、裘、馬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twentieth year, when the Yongle Emperor personally campaigned beyond the passes, Mengge Buhua led his sons and younger brothers and his followers to join; he was granted bows and arrows, furs, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongle 20, on another personal campaign beyond the frontier, Mengge Buhua followed with his kin and troops and received bows, furs, and horses as gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三月，成祖復親征出塞，猛哥不花使所屬指揮僉事王吉從，成祖嘉賚之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-second year, when the Yongle Emperor again personally campaigned beyond the passes, Mengge Buhua sent his subordinate assistant commander Wang Ji to follow; the Yongle Emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongle 22, on yet another imperial campaign, Mengge Buhua sent his assistant commander Wang Ji; the emperor commended and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 七月，成祖崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Yongle Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Yongle Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年正月，猛哥不花、猛哥帖木兒朝於明。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xuande, Mengge Buhua and Mengge Timur presented themselves at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xuande 1, Mengge Buhua and Mengge Timur came to court.

sentences.zh: 是月壬子，進猛哥帖木兒爲都督僉事。

translations.literal: That month on renzi day, Mengge Timur was advanced to assistant regional military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That month, on a renzi day, Mengge Timur was promoted to assistant regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 釋加奴已前卒，三月辛丑，以其子李滿住爲都督僉事。

translations.literal: Shi Jianu had already died earlier; on xinchou day of the third month, his son Li Manzhu was made assistant regional military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu had died earlier; on the xinchou day of the third month his son Li Manzhu was appointed assistant regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳，進猛哥不花爲中軍都督同知，仍掌毛憐衞。

translations.literal: On dingsi day of the ninth month, Mengge Buhua was advanced to vice commissioner of the Central Military Commission and continued to administer the Maolian Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the ninth month Mengge Buhua was made vice commissioner of the Central Military Commission while retaining command of the Maolian Guard.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，猛哥不花使貢馬，旋卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Mengge Buhua sent tribute horses and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xuande 2 he sent horses as tribute and soon afterward died.

sentences.zh: 四月，命餼其孥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, an order was issued to provision his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the court ordered provisions for his family.

sentences.zh: 猛哥不花子二：撒滿哈失里、官保奴。

translations.literal: Mengge Buhua had two sons: Samanhashili and Guanbaonu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengge Buhua left two sons, Samanhashili and Guanbaonu.

sentences.zh: 撒滿哈失里蒙其祖阿哈出賜姓爲李氏，四年三月壬子，明以爲都督僉事。

translations.literal: Samanhashili, owing to his grandfather A Ha Chu's granted surname, was of the Li clan; on renzi day of the third month of the fourth year, the Ming made him assistant regional military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Samanhashili bore the Li surname granted to his grandfather A Ha Chu; on a renzi day in the third month of Xuande 4 the Ming appointed him assistant regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，官保奴朝於明。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, Guanbaonu presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xuande 5, Guanbaonu came to court.

sentences.zh: 四月，李滿住上言求市於朝鮮，朝鮮不納，宣宗敕諭聽於遼東境上通市。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Li Manzhu submitted a memorial requesting trade with Korea; Korea would not accept it; the Xuande Emperor issued an edict ordering that trade be permitted on the Liaodong border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Manzhu asked permission to trade with Korea; when Korea refused, the Xuande Emperor directed that markets be opened on the Liaodong frontier instead.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，釋加奴妻唐氏朝於明。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, Shi Jianu's wife, Lady Tang, presented herself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xuande 6, Shi Jianu's widow Lady Tang came to court.

sentences.zh: 二月，撒滿哈失里朝於明。

translations.literal: In the second month, Samanhashili presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Samanhashili came to court.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，猛哥帖木兒使其弟凡察朝於明；

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, Mengge Timur sent his younger brother Fancha to present himself at the Ming court;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xuande 7, Mengge Timur sent his brother Fancha to court;

sentences.zh: 三月壬戌，明以爲都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: on renxu day of the third month, the Ming made him assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: and on a renxu day in the third month the Ming appointed him assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 八年二月庚戌，進猛哥帖木兒爲右都督，凡察都指揮使。

translations.literal: On gengxu day of the second month of the eighth year, Mengge Timur was advanced to right regional commander and Fancha to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the second month of Xuande 8, Mengge Timur was promoted to right regional commander and Fancha to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 六月，撒滿哈失里朝於明。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Samanhashili presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Samanhashili came to court.

sentences.zh: 是年，七姓野人木答忽等糾阿速江等衞頭人弗答哈等掠建州衛，殺左衞都督猛哥帖木兒及其子阿古，凡察告難於明。

translations.literal: That year, the Seven-clan wild Jurchens, Mudahu and others, together with the headmen Fudaha and others of the Asujiang and other guards, raided Jianzhou; they killed the Left Guard regional commander Mengge Timur and his son Agu; Fancha reported the disaster to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Seven-clan wild Jurchens under Mudahu, with chiefs such as Fudaha of the Asujiang guard, raided Jianzhou and killed Left Guard commander Mengge Timur and his son Agu. Fancha reported the calamity to the Ming court.

sentences.zh: 會明使都指揮裴俊如斡木河，中途遇寇，凡察以所屬赴援，有功。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ming envoy, regional commander Pei Jun, was going to the Wumu River and encountered bandits midway; Fancha led his followers to the rescue and performed meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming envoy Pei Jun was traveling to the Wumu River and met raiders on the way, Fancha brought his men to aid him and won merit.

sentences.zh: 九年二月癸酉，進凡察都督僉事，掌衞事，敕諭木答忽等還所掠人、馬、貲財，且赦其罪。

translations.literal: On guiyou day of the second month of the ninth year, Fancha was advanced to assistant regional commissioner and placed in charge of guard affairs; an edict ordered Mudahu and others to return the people, horses, and goods they had seized and also pardoned their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On a guiyou day in the second month of Xuande 9, Fancha was made assistant regional commissioner and put in charge of the guard. An edict commanded Mudahu and his allies to return captives, horses, and plunder and granted them pardon.

sentences.zh: 是月，撒滿哈失里母金阿納失里朝於明。

translations.literal: That month, Samanhashili's mother, Jin'anashili, presented herself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: That month Samanhashili's mother Jin'anashili came to court.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年正月，宣宗崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year of Xuande, the Xuande Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xuande 10 the Xuande Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 是月，李滿住、撒滿哈失里上言忽剌溫境內野人那列禿等掠所屬那顏寨，敕諭那列禿等還所掠人、馬、貲財，並以責弗答哈等。

translations.literal: That month, Li Manzhu and Samanhashili submitted memorials that the wild Jurchens Nalietu and others within Hurka territory had raided their subordinates' Nayanzhai; an edict ordered Nalietu and others to return the people, horses, and goods seized, and Fudaha and others were also rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Manzhu and Samanhashili reported that Hurka tribesmen led by Nalietu had raided the Nayanzhai settlement. An edict ordered the return of captives and loot and rebuked Fudaha and his associates as well.

sentences.zh: 四月，撒滿哈失里朝於明。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Samanhashili presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Samanhashili came to court.

sentences.zh: 正統元年閏六月，李滿住使其子古納哈等朝於明，還遼東逃人，明英宗嘉其效誠，賜採緞、冠服；

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month of the first year of Zhengtong, Li Manzhu sent his son Gunaha and others to present themselves at the Ming court and returned fugitives from Liaodong; the Ming Emperor Yingzong praised their loyal service and granted figured silks and court dress;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month of Zhengtong 1, Li Manzhu sent his son Gunaha and others to court, returning Liaodong fugitives. Emperor Yingzong commended their loyalty and gave figured silks and court robes;

sentences.zh: 並上章言忽剌溫野人相侵，乞徙居遼陽婆猪江，英宗命遼東總兵官巫凱計議安置，毋弛邊備，毋失夷情。

translations.literal: and also submitted a memorial stating that Hurka wild Jurchens were encroaching and requesting relocation to the Pozhu River in Liaoyang; Emperor Yingzong ordered the Liaodong supreme commander Wu Kai to deliberate on resettlement, without relaxing border defenses or losing the goodwill of the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: they also petitioned that Hurka raiders were pressing them and asked to move to the Pozhu River in Liaoyang. Yingzong told supreme commander Wu Kai to plan the resettlement without weakening the frontier or alienating the tribes.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，凡察使所屬指揮同知李伍哈朝於明，上章言：「居鄰朝鮮，爲所困；

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Fancha sent his subordinate commander Li Wuha to present himself at the Ming court; he submitted a memorial stating: "We dwell neighboring Korea and are harassed by them;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengtong 2, Fancha sent his commander Li Wuha to court with a memorial: "We live beside Korea and suffer their pressure;

sentences.zh: 欲還建州，又爲所阻：乞朝命。

translations.literal: we wish to return to Jianzhou but are again obstructed: we beg an imperial command."
translations.idiomatic: we wish to return to Jianzhou but are blocked again—we beg the court's command."

sentences.zh: 」英宗賜敕撫諭。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yingzong granted an edict to comfort and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong replied with a comforting edict.

sentences.zh: 五月，撒滿哈失里朝於明，自陳原留京師自効。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Samanhashili presented himself at the Ming court and stated of his own accord that he wished to remain in the capital to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Samanhashili came to court and volunteered to stay in the capital in imperial service.

sentences.zh: 前，撒滿哈失里已進都督同知，英宗命仍掌毛憐衞事，賜敕遣之。

translations.literal: Previously, Samanhashili had already been advanced to vice regional commissioner; Emperor Yingzong ordered him still to administer Maolian Guard affairs, granted an edict, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Samanhashili had already been promoted to vice regional commissioner; Yingzong ordered him to keep charge of the Maolian Guard, gave him an edict, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 是時，李滿住掌建州衞，凡察掌建州左衞，與撒滿哈失里並奉職貢惟謹。

translations.literal: At this time, Li Manzhu administered the Jianzhou Guard, Fancha the Left Jianzhou Guard, and together with Samanhashili they all fulfilled their duties and tribute with scrupulous care.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Manzhu held Jianzhou, Fancha held Left Jianzhou, and Samanhashili held Maolian; all three punctiliously performed duty and tribute.

sentences.zh: 而故建州左衞都督猛哥帖木兒死七姓野人之難，子阿古殉焉，諸子董山、綽顏依凡察以居。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the former Left Jianzhou regional commander Mengge Timur had died in the calamity of the Seven-clan wild Jurchens; his son Agu died with him; his other sons Dongshan and Chuoyan lived under Fancha's protection.
translations.idiomatic: The former Left Jianzhou commander Mengge Timur had perished in the Seven-clan raid; his son Agu died with him, and his sons Dongshan and Chuoyan now lived under Fancha's care.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，以董山爲本衞指揮使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, Dongshan was made commander of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year Dongshan was appointed commander of the guard.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，凡察朝於明。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Fancha presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengtong 3, Fancha came to court.

sentences.zh: 是月壬子，英宗賜以敕曰：「往者猛哥帖木兒死七姓野人之難，失其印，宣德間，別鑄印畀凡察。

translations.literal: That month on renzi day, Emperor Yingzong granted an edict stating: "Formerly Mengge Timur died in the calamity of the Seven-clan wild Jurchens and lost his seal; during the Xuande reign a new seal was cast and given to Fancha.
translations.idiomatic: That month, on a renzi day, Yingzong issued an edict: "When Mengge Timur fell in the Seven-clan disaster his seal was lost; in the Xuande era a new seal was cast for Fancha.

sentences.zh: 董山上言舊印故在，而凡察復請留新印。

translations.literal: Dongshan submitted a memorial that the old seal still existed, while Fancha again requested to keep the new seal.
translations.idiomatic: Dongshan reported that the old seal still survived, while Fancha again asked to keep the new one.

sentences.zh: 一衞二印無故事。

translations.literal: One guard with two seals has no precedent.
translations.idiomatic: There is no precedent for two seals in one guard.

sentences.zh: 敕至，爾等協同署事，遣使上舊印。

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, you shall jointly administer affairs and send envoys to surrender the old seal.
translations.idiomatic: When this edict arrives, administer affairs jointly and send the old seal up to the court.

sentences.zh: 」凡察、董山爭衞印自此始。

translations.literal: " From this the dispute between Fancha and Dongshan over the guard seal began.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Fancha and Dongshan began their struggle over the guard seal.

sentences.zh: 六月，李滿住使所屬指揮趙歹因哈上章，言：「自徙居婆猪江，屢爲朝鮮侵掠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Li Manzhu sent his subordinate commander Zhao Daiyinha to submit a memorial stating: "Since we relocated to the Pozhu River, we have repeatedly been raided by Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Manzhu sent his commander Zhao Daiyinha with a memorial: "Since our move to the Pozhu River we have suffered repeated Korean raids.

sentences.zh: 今復徙居竈突山東南渾河上，爲朝廷守邊圉，罔敢或違。

translations.literal: We now relocate again to the Hun River southeast of Zaotu Mountain to guard the border for the court and dare not disobey in the least."
translations.idiomatic: We now move again to the Hun River southeast of Zaotu Mountain to guard the frontier for the throne and would not dream of defying your will."

sentences.zh: 」別疏又言：「毛憐衞印爲指揮阿里所匿，請別鑄印畀撒滿哈失里。

translations.literal: " A separate memorial also stated: "The Maolian Guard seal is concealed by the commander Ali; I request a separate seal be cast and given to Samanhashili."
translations.idiomatic: A separate petition added: "Commander Ali has hidden the Maolian seal—please cast a new one for Samanhashili."

sentences.zh: 」英宗不許，命撒滿哈失里奏事，附李滿住以達。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yingzong did not approve and ordered that Samanhashili submit memorials attached to Li Manzhu's communications for delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong refused and directed Samanhashili to route his petitions through Li Manzhu.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，李滿住上言：「都督凡察、指揮童倉爲朝鮮所誘，叛去。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Li Manzhu submitted a memorial: "Regional commander Fancha and commander Tong Cang were enticed by Korea and have defected.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhengtong 4, Li Manzhu reported that regional commander Fancha and commander Tong Cang had been lured by Korea and had defected.

sentences.zh: 」童倉即董山，譯音異也。

translations.literal: " Tong Cang is Dongshan—the difference is only in transliteration.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Cang and Dongshan are the same man; only the transcription differs.

sentences.zh: 英宗敕朝鮮國王李祹問狀，祹疏自明非誘。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong ordered the King of Korea, Li Xiang, to investigate; Li Xiang's memorial clarified of his own accord that there had been no enticement.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong ordered King Li Xiang of Korea to investigate; Li Xiang's memorial denied any enticement.

sentences.zh: 英宗命凡察、童倉即居鏡城，復敕祹撫諭之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong ordered Fancha and Tong Cang to reside at once in Gyeongseong and again instructed Li Xiang to comfort and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong ordered Fancha and Tong Cang to stay in Gyeongseong and told Li Xiang to treat them well.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，英宗以李滿住與福餘衞韃靼相侵盜，敕遼東總兵曹義備邊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, because Li Manzhu and the Tatars of the Fuyu Guard were mutually raiding and plundering, Emperor Yingzong ordered the Liaodong supreme commander Cao Yi to prepare border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhengtong 5, with Li Manzhu and the Fuyu Guard Tatars raiding each other, Yingzong ordered supreme commander Cao Yi to ready the frontier.

sentences.zh: 九月，朝鮮國王李祹上言凡察、童倉復逃還建州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the King of Korea, Li Xiang, submitted a memorial that Fancha and Tong Cang had again fled back to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month King Li Xiang reported that Fancha and Tong Cang had fled back to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 總兵曹義亦疏陳：「凡察等去鏡城，率叛軍馬哈剌等四十家至蘇子河，乏食。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Cao Yi also submitted a memorial stating: "Fancha and the others left Gyeongseong, leading the deserter Mahala and forty other households to the Suzi River, and lack food."
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Cao Yi also reported: "Fancha and his party left Gyeongseong with the deserter Mahala and forty households, reached the Suzi River, and are short of food."

sentences.zh: 」英宗敕義使編置三土河及婆猪江迤西冬古河兩界間，仍依李滿住以居，發粟賑之；

translations.literal: " Emperor Yingzong ordered Yi to arrange their settlement between the Santu River and the Donggu River west of the Pozhu River, still placing them under Li Manzhu's jurisdiction, and to distribute grain in relief;
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong told Yi to resettle them between the Santu and Donggu rivers west of the Pozhu River, still under Li Manzhu's authority, and to issue grain relief;

sentences.zh: 貰逃軍馬哈剌等，命還伍。

translations.literal: the deserter Mahala and others were pardoned and ordered to return to their units.
translations.idiomatic: Mahala and the other deserters were pardoned and ordered back to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 復諭祹使歸其種人留朝鮮境者。

translations.literal: Li Xiang was again instructed to return his tribesmen who remained within Korean territory.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang was also told to send back any of their people still in Korea.

sentences.zh: 是時，凡察以都督、董山以指揮同領建州左衞，其徙居鏡城復還。

translations.literal: At this time Fancha as regional commander and Dongshan as commander jointly led the Left Jianzhou Guard; they had relocated to Gyeongseong and returned again.
translations.idiomatic: Fancha now held the rank of regional commander and Dongshan that of commander, jointly leading Left Jianzhou after their sojourn in Gyeongseong and return.

sentences.zh: 六年正月戊午，進董山爲都督僉事。

translations.literal: On wuwu day of the first month of the sixth year, Dongshan was advanced to assistant regional commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the first month of Zhengtong 6, Dongshan was promoted to assistant regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月，朝鮮國王李祹上言：「凡察舊居鏡城阿木河，其兄猛哥帖木兒，臣祖授以萬戶，創公廨，與婢僕、衣糧、鞍馬，臣父又授以上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second month, the King of Korea, Li Xiang, submitted a memorial: "Fancha formerly dwelt at the Amu River in Gyeongseong; his elder brother Mengge Timur—my grandfather granted him the rank of myriarch, built a public office, and gave servants, clothing, grain, and saddle horses; my father further granted him Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month King Li Xiang memorialized: "Fancha once lived on the Amu River at Gyeongseong. His brother Mengge Timur received from my grandfather the rank of myriarch, a government compound, servants, provisions, and horses; my father later made him Senior General.

sentences.zh: 及死七姓野人之難，其子阿古殉焉，屋宇、貲產焚掠殆盡。

translations.literal: When he died in the calamity of the Seven-clan wild Jurchens, his son Agu died with him; dwellings and property were burned and plundered almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When he died in the Seven-clan disaster his son Agu perished with him, and their houses and goods were nearly all burned and looted.

sentences.zh: 臣撫卹凡察，如先臣撫卹其兄。

translations.literal: I comforted and supported Fancha as my forebears had comforted and supported his brother.
translations.idiomatic: I supported Fancha as my forebears had supported his brother.

sentences.zh: 近歲徙居東良，後乃潛逃，與李滿住同處。

translations.literal: In recent years he moved to Dongliang, then secretly fled and dwells together with Li Manzhu.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years he moved to Dongliang, then slipped away and now lives with Li Manzhu.

sentences.zh: 此時臣不及知，安有追殺？

translations.literal: At that time I did not know in time—how could there have been pursuit and killing?
translations.idiomatic: I learned of it only afterward—how could I have pursued and killed them?

sentences.zh: 或有留者，非懷土不去，則同類開諭而還，非臣阻之也。

translations.literal: If any remained, it was not because they clung to the land and would not leave, or because their kin persuaded them to return—it was not because I obstructed them.
translations.idiomatic: If any stayed behind, it was from attachment to the land or persuasion by their kin—not because I blocked their return.

sentences.zh: 李滿住昔居婆猪江，在臣國邊境。

translations.literal: Li Manzhu formerly dwelt on the Pozhu River, on my state's border.
translations.idiomatic: Li Manzhu once lived on the Pozhu River along our border.

sentences.zh: 鹽米醯醬隨其所索，時時給與。

translations.literal: Salt, rice, vinegar, and sauce—whatever they requested were supplied from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: We supplied salt, grain, vinegar, and sauce whenever they asked.

sentences.zh: 後引忽剌溫劫掠臣邊不已。

translations.literal: Later he brought Hurka raiders to plunder my border without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Later he brought Hurka raiders to harry our frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 今凡察與同惡，謀與忽剌溫等來侵。

translations.literal: Now Fancha shares his wickedness and plots with Hurka and others to come and invade.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fancha joins his malice and plots with the Hurka to invade us.

sentences.zh: 請飭凡察等遄返舊居，庶小國邊民獲免寇盜。

translations.literal: I request that Fancha and others be ordered to return quickly to their former dwellings, so that the border people of this small state may be spared raids and banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Please order Fancha and his party to return at once to their old homes, so our border people may be spared raids.

sentences.zh: 」英宗敕祹謹爲備。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yingzong instructed Li Xiang to prepare defenses carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong told Li Xiang to stand ready on his guard.

sentences.zh: 會凡察上言不敢爲非，敕遼東總兵曹義遣使諭之，並廉其情偽。

translations.literal: It happened that Fancha submitted a memorial stating he dared not do wrong; the Liaodong supreme commander Cao Yi was ordered to send envoys to instruct him and also to investigate the truth of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Fancha memorialized that he would not misbehave, Yingzong ordered supreme commander Cao Yi to send envoys to warn him and ascertain the truth.

sentences.zh: 凡察、董山爭衞印數年而不決。

translations.literal: Fancha and Dongshan's dispute over the guard seal continued for years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Fancha and Dongshan's fight over the guard seal dragged on unresolved for years.

sentences.zh: 七年二月甲辰，英宗用總兵官曹義議，析置建州右衞，凡察、董山皆進都督同知，董山以舊印掌左衞，凡察以新印掌右衞，敕分領所屬，守法安業，毋事爭鬭。

translations.literal: On jiachen day of the second month of the seventh year, Emperor Yingzong adopted supreme commander Cao Yi's proposal, separately established the Right Jianzhou Guard, advanced both Fancha and Dongshan to vice regional commissioner—Dongshan with the old seal to administer the Left Guard, Fancha with the new seal the Right Guard—and ordered them to divide their followers, observe the law, settle in peace, and not engage in strife.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiachen day in the second month of Zhengtong 7, Yingzong followed Cao Yi's advice and split off Right Jianzhou. Fancha and Dongshan were both promoted to vice regional commissioner: Dongshan kept the old seal for Left Jianzhou, Fancha the new seal for Right Jianzhou. They were told to divide their followers, keep the peace, and cease fighting.

sentences.zh: 董山、凡察及李滿住各爲所屬乞官，皆許之。

translations.literal: Dongshan, Fancha, and Li Manzhu each requested offices for their subordinates—all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Dongshan, Fancha, and Li Manzhu all petitioned for commissions for their men, and all were approved.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲有干請。

translations.literal: From this time forward, each year there were petitions.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they petitioned every year.

sentences.zh: 久次，乞進秩；

translations.literal: After long service at court, they requested advancement in rank;
translations.idiomatic: After long stays at court they sought promotion;

sentences.zh: 物故，乞襲職，以爲常。

translations.literal: on death, they requested inheritance of office—this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: When a man died, his heirs petitioned to inherit his post, and this became routine.

sentences.zh: 撒滿哈失里朝於明。

translations.literal: Samanhashili presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: Samanhashili came to court.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，進右都督，別鑄毛憐衞印畀之。

translations.literal: On dingchou day of the third month, he was advanced to right regional commander; a separate Maolian Guard seal was cast and given to him.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingchou day in the third month he was promoted to right regional commander and given a newly cast Maolian seal.

sentences.zh: 五月，英宗以凡察等屢言朝鮮留其部眾，使錦衣衞指揮僉事吳良齎敕往勘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, because Fancha and others repeatedly stated that Korea was detaining their tribesmen, Emperor Yingzong sent the Jinyi Guard assistant commander Wu Liang bearing an edict to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, after Fancha and others repeatedly complained that Korea was holding their people, Yingzong sent Jinyi Guard officer Wu Liang with an edict to investigate.

sentences.zh: 凡察所索童哈阿里等，居朝鮮久，受職事，守丘墓，皆自陳不願還，而以十人還李滿住。

translations.literal: Those Fancha sought—Tongha Ali and others—had lived long in Korea, received offices, and guarded ancestral tombs; all stated of their own accord that they did not wish to return, and only ten men were returned to Li Manzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Those Fancha wanted—men such as Tongha Ali—had lived in Korea for years, held offices there, and tended graves; they all said they would not return, and only ten men were sent back to Li Manzhu.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，李滿住使報兀良哈將入寇，英宗命僉都御史王翱勒兵爲備。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year, Li Manzhu's envoy reported that the Uriankhai were about to invade; Emperor Yingzong ordered the vice censor-in-chief Wang Ao to muster troops in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhengtong 8, an envoy from Li Manzhu warned that the Uriankhai were preparing to raid. Yingzong ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Ao to mobilize troops on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，李滿住等上言指揮郎克苦等還自朝鮮，乞賑，英宗命發粟賑之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, Li Manzhu and others memorialized that the commander Langkeku and others had returned from Korea and begged relief; Emperor Yingzong ordered grain issued to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengtong 9, Li Manzhu and others reported that Commander Langkeku and his party had come back from Korea and needed relief. Yingzong ordered grain distributed to them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，董山、凡察朝於明。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Dongshan and Fancha presented themselves at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Dongshan and Fancha came to court.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，撒滿哈失里朝於明。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, Samanhashili presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengtong 10, Samanhashili came to court.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，以董山弟綽顏爲副千戶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year, Dongshan's younger brother Chuoyan was made deputy chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhengtong 11, Dongshan's brother Chuoyan was appointed deputy chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，進李滿住爲都督同知。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Li Manzhu was advanced to vice regional commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengtong 12, Li Manzhu was promoted to vice regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六月，以聞瓦剌將寇邊，敕建州三衞李滿住、董山、凡察等使爲備。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on hearing that the Oirats were about to raid the border, an edict ordered Li Manzhu, Dongshan, Fancha, and others of the Jianzhou Three Guards to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, after word that the Oirats would strike the frontier, the court ordered Li Manzhu, Dongshan, Fancha, and the other Jianzhou Three Guard leaders to ready their defenses.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，復敕戒李滿住等毋為北虜誘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, an edict again admonished Li Manzhu and others not to be enticed by the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengtong 13, the court again warned Li Manzhu and his fellows not to let the northern enemies draw them in.

sentences.zh: 十二月，董山、凡察朝於明。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Dongshan and Fancha presented themselves at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Dongshan and Fancha again came to court.

sentences.zh: 十四年，凡察妻朶兒眞索朝於明，進皇太后塔納珠二顆，賚以紵絲表裏。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Fancha's wife Duorerzhen Suo presented herself at the Ming court, presented two tanazhu pearls to the empress dowager, and was rewarded with lined ramie silks.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 14, Fancha's wife Duorerzhen Suo came to court, offered the empress dowager two tanazhu pearls, and received lined ramie robes in return.

sentences.zh: 既而額森入寇，建州三衞亦屢犯邊。

translations.literal: Thereafter Esen invaded, and the Jianzhou Three Guards also repeatedly violated the border.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Esen launched his invasion, and the Jianzhou Three Guards raided the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，王翱巡撫遠東，使招諭，復叩關。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign, Wang Ao as grand coordinator of the remote east sent envoys to summon and instruct them, and they again knocked at the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingtai years Wang Ao, as grand coordinator of the far northeast, sent men to win them back, and they resumed coming to the frontier gates.

sentences.zh: 天順二年正月，李滿住朝於明。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tianshun, Li Manzhu presented himself at the Ming court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianshun 2, Li Manzhu came to court.

sentences.zh: 二月，進董山右都督。

translations.literal: In the second month, Dongshan was advanced to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Dongshan was promoted to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 時董山陰附朝鮮，朝鮮授以中樞密使。

translations.literal: At this time Dongshan secretly aligned with Korea, and Korea invested him as Central Secretariat commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Dongshan had been dealing secretly with Korea, which had made him a Central Secretariat commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巡撫遼東都御史程信詗得其制書以聞，英宗使詰朝鮮及董山，皆慴服，貢馬謝。

translations.literal: The Liaodong grand coordinator and censor-in-chief Cheng Xin inquired and obtained his commission document and reported it; Emperor Yingzong sent to interrogate Korea and Dongshan; all were awed into submission and presented horses in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong grand coordinator Cheng Xin investigated, seized Dongshan's Korean commission, and reported it. Yingzong summoned Korea and Dongshan to account; both submitted in fear and sent horses in apology.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，朝鮮國王李瑈上言：「建州眾夜至義州江，殺並江收禾民，掠男婦、牛馬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, the king of Korea Li Rui memorialized: "Jianzhou tribesmen came by night to the Yizhou River, killed the people harvesting grain along the river, and carried off men, women, cattle, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianshun 5, King Li Rui of Korea reported: "Jianzhou raiders came by night to the Yizhou River, killed farmers gathering the harvest along the banks, and seized men, women, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 」下兵部議，以爲朝鮮嘗誘殺毛憐衞都督郎卜兒哈，致寇乃自取，置勿問。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of War for deliberation; it was held that Korea had once lured and killed the Maolian Guard regional commander Langboerha, so the raids were self-invited, and the case was left unattended.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of War reviewed the complaint and ruled that Korea had once lured and killed Maolian commander Langboerha, so these raids were of its own making; no action was taken.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月，英宗崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the eighth year, Emperor Yingzong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in Tianshun 8, Yingzong died.

sentences.zh: 成化元年正月，董山朝於明，自陳防邊有勞，乞進秩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Chenghua, Dongshan presented himself at the Ming court, stated of his own accord that he had merit in defending the border, and begged advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chenghua 1, Dongshan came to court, claimed credit for frontier defense, and asked for promotion.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不許，賜以採緞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong did not grant it and bestowed figured satin instead.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong refused the promotion and gave him figured satin instead.

sentences.zh: 十月，整飭邊備。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, border defenses were reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court reorganized frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 左都御史李秉上言：「建州、毛憐、海西諸部落入貢，邊臣驗方物，貂必純黑，馬必肥大，否則拒不納。

translations.literal: The left censor-in-chief Li Bing memorialized: "When the Jianzhou, Maolian, and Haixi tribes come to offer tribute, border officials inspect the goods: sables must be pure black and horses must be fat and large, or they are refused.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Li Bing reported: "When Jianzhou, Maolian, and Haixi tribes bring tribute, frontier officials inspect the goods—sables must be jet black and horses stout, or the gifts are rejected.

sentences.zh: 今諸部落結福餘三衞屢犯邊，貢使至，使者不宜過持擇，召邊釁。

translations.literal: Now the tribes have joined the Fuyu Three Guards in repeatedly violating the border; when tribute envoys arrive, the envoys should not be overly choosy, lest they provoke border incidents."
translations.idiomatic: Now those tribes have allied with the Fuyu Three Guards in repeated raids. When tribute missions arrive, officials should not be so exacting—that only invites trouble on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗命從之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xianzong ordered that his proposal be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong approved the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，秉上言：「毛憐諸衞犯邊，官兵擊破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, Li Bing memorialized: "The Maolian guards violated the border and government troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Chenghua 2, Li Bing reported: "Maolian guards had raided the frontier and government troops had beaten them back.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，復入犯，總兵武安侯鄭宏戰敗。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month they invaded again, and the supreme commander, Marquis of Wu'an Zheng Hong, was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month they struck again, and supreme commander Zheng Hong, Marquis of Wu'an, was defeated.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，秉上言：「董山歸所掠邊人，請贖俘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Li Bing memorialized: "Dongshan has returned the border people he seized and asks to ransom captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chenghua 3, Li Bing reported: "Dongshan has returned the frontier people he took and asks to ransom his prisoners.

sentences.zh: 」憲宗敕獎董山，因戒責建州、毛憐諸衞，旋使錦衣衞署都督僉事武忠將命撫諭。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xianzong issued an edict commending Dongshan and admonishing the Jianzhou and Maolian guards, then soon sent the Jinyi Guard acting regional vice commissioner Wu Zhong bearing orders to pacify and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong praised Dongshan in an edict, rebuked the Jianzhou and Maolian guards, and soon dispatched Jinyi Guard officer Wu Zhong to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 是月，海西、建州諸衞復入鴉鶻關，都指揮鄧佐禦諸雙嶺，中伏死，副總兵施英不能救。

translations.literal: That month the Haixi and Jianzhou guards again entered Yahuguan Pass; the regional commander Deng Zuo defended them at Shuangling, fell into an ambush and died, and the deputy supreme commander Shi Ying could not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: That month Haixi and Jianzhou forces again broke through Yahuguan. Regional commander Deng Zuo met them at Shuangling, was ambushed and killed, and deputy commander Shi Ying could not save him.

sentences.zh: 三月，復入連山關，掠開原、撫順，窺鐵嶺、寧遠、廣寧。

translations.literal: In the third month they again entered Lianshan Pass, plundered Kaiyuan and Fushun, and spied on Tieling, Ningyuan, and Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they broke through Lianshan Pass again, raided Kaiyuan and Fushun, and probed toward Tieling, Ningyuan, and Guangning.

sentences.zh: 及忠至，董山等受撫。

translations.literal: When Wu Zhong arrived, Dongshan and the others accepted pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu Zhong arrived, Dongshan and his party submitted to pacification.

sentences.zh: 四月，偕李古納哈等朝於明，憲宗使集闕下，宣詔赦其罪，董山等頓首聽命。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, together with Li Gunaha and others, he presented himself at the Ming court; Emperor Xianzong had them assemble below the palace gate, proclaimed an edict pardoning their crimes, and Dongshan and the others kowtowed and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Dongshan came to court with Li Gunaha and others. Xianzong assembled them below the palace, proclaimed a pardon, and they kowtowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 五月己丑，復以左都御史李秉提督軍務，武靖伯趙輔佩靖虜將軍印，充總兵官，發兵討建州，而董山等留京師，會賜宴，其從者語嫚，奪庖人銅牌，事聞，有詔切責；

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the fifth month, the left censor-in-chief Li Bing was again made military superintendent, the Wujing Earl Zhao Fu was given the Pacify-Barbarians general's seal and made supreme commander, and troops were sent to punish Jianzhou; meanwhile Dongshan and others remained in the capital, and at a feast granted to them their followers used insulting speech and seized the cook's bronze tally; when the matter was reported, a stern edict rebuked them;
translations.idiomatic: On a jichou day in the fifth month Li Bing was again put in charge of military affairs, Zhao Fu was given the Pacify-Barbarians seal as supreme commander, and an expedition was launched against Jianzhou. Dongshan and his party stayed in the capital; at a court feast their followers were insolent and seized a cook's bronze tally. When word reached the throne, Xianzong rebuked them sharply;

sentences.zh: 既而，予馬值、賚綵幣如故事。

translations.literal: thereafter horse compensation was granted and colored silks bestowed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: they were then given horse compensation and silks as usual.

sentences.zh: 董山、李古納哈乞蟒衣、玉帶、金頂帽、銀酒器，憲宗命增賜衣、帽，人一具。

translations.literal: Dongshan and Li Gunaha begged python robes, jade belts, gold-topped caps, and silver wine vessels; Emperor Xianzong ordered additional gifts of robes and caps, one set per man.
translations.idiomatic: Dongshan and Li Gunaha asked for python robes, jade belts, gold-topped caps, and silver wine sets. Xianzong added robes and caps—one set for each man.

sentences.zh: 董山又言指揮可昆等五人有勞，乞賜，憲宗命賜衣，人一襲。

translations.literal: Dongshan further stated that the commander Kokun and five others had merit and begged gifts; Emperor Xianzong ordered robes granted, one garment per man.
translations.idiomatic: Dongshan also said that Commander Kokun and four others had served well and deserved rewards. Xianzong gave each of the five a robe.

sentences.zh: 董山等辭歸，鴻臚寺通事署丞王忠奏：「董山等罵坐不敬，貪求無厭，揚言歸且復叛，請遣官防送。

translations.literal: When Dongshan and the others took leave to return, the Honglu Temple junior clerk Wang Zhong memorialized: "Dongshan and the others cursed at their seats without respect, were insatiably greedy in their requests, and declared that on returning they would rebel again; I beg that officials be sent to escort them under guard.
translations.idiomatic: As Dongshan and his party prepared to leave, Honglu Temple clerk Wang Zhong reported: "Dongshan and his men insulted their hosts at the feast, demanded gifts without end, and boasted they would rebel again once home. I ask that officials escort them under guard.

sentences.zh: 」憲宗命禮部遣行人護行，復賜敕戒諭。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xianzong ordered the Ministry of Rites to send a messenger to escort them on the journey and again granted an edict of admonition and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong ordered the Ministry of Rites to send an escort and issued another admonishing edict.

sentences.zh: 董山等既行，憲宗復用禮部主事高岡議，命趙輔縶董山塞上。

translations.literal: After Dongshan and the others had set out, Emperor Xianzong again adopted the proposal of the Ministry of Rites clerk Gao Gang and ordered Zhao Fu to detain Dongshan on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After Dongshan and his party had left, Xianzong took up a proposal from Ministry of Rites clerk Gao Gang and ordered Zhao Fu to seize Dongshan on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 輔留董山等廣寧，令遣使戒所屬毋更盜邊。

translations.literal: Zhao Fu detained Dongshan and the others at Guangning and ordered them to send envoys warning their subordinates not to raid the border again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fu held Dongshan and his men at Guangning and told them to send word to their followers not to raid the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 七月庚申，輔召董山等聽宣敕，未畢，董山等爲嫚語，袖出刃刺譯者，吏士格鬭，殺董山等二十六人。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the seventh month, Zhao Fu summoned Dongshan and the others to hear the edict proclaimed; before it was finished, Dongshan and the others used insulting speech, drew blades from their sleeves and stabbed the interpreter, clerks and soldiers grappled with them, and Dongshan and twenty-six others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengshen day in the seventh month Zhao Fu summoned Dongshan and his party to hear an edict. Before the reading ended they grew abusive, pulled hidden blades, and stabbed the interpreter. In the brawl that followed Dongshan and twenty-six of his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗命發兵益秉、輔東征，敕安撫毛憐、海西諸衞，示專討建州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong ordered troops sent to reinforce Li Bing and Zhao Fu in the eastern campaign, issued an edict to pacify the Maolian and Haixi guards, and showed that the strike was aimed solely at Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong reinforced Li Bing and Zhao Fu for the eastern campaign, pacified the Maolian and Haixi guards by edict, and made clear that only Jianzhou was the target.

sentences.zh: 九月，分道出師：左軍渡渾河，越石門，至分水嶺；

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army marched by separate routes: the left wing crossed the Hun River, passed Shimen, and reached the Watershed Ridge;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army advanced in three columns: the left wing crossed the Hun River, passed Shimen, and reached the Watershed Ridge;

sentences.zh: 右軍度鴉鶻關，踰鳳凰城、摩天嶺，至婆猪江；

translations.literal: the right wing passed through Yahuguan, crossed Fenghuangcheng and Motian Ridge, and reached the Pozhu River;
translations.idiomatic: the right wing went through Yahuguan, crossed Fenghuangcheng and Motian Ridge, and reached the Pozhu River;

sentences.zh: 中軍下撫順，經薄刀山，過五嶺，渡蘇子河，至虎城。

translations.literal: the center army descended on Fushun, passed through Boqian Mountain, crossed the Five Ridges, forded the Suzi River, and reached Hucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The center column marched down on Fushun, crossed Boqian Mountain and the Five Ridges, forded the Suzi River, and came to Hucheng.

sentences.zh: 攻破張打必納、戴咬納、朗家、嘹哈諸寨，四戰皆捷。

translations.literal: they stormed the stockades at Zhangdabina, Daiyaona, Langjia, and Liaoha; all four battles were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: They overran the stockades at Zhangdabina, Daiyaona, Langjia, and Liaoha, winning every one of four engagements.

sentences.zh: 十月，師還。

translations.literal: in the tenth month, the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秉上疏請增兵戍遼陽，於鳳凰山、鴉鶻關、撫順、奉集、通遠諸路，度地築城堡，選將吏習邊事者鎭開原，憲宗悉從之。

translations.literal: Bing memorialized requesting increased troops to garrison Liaoyang; at Fenghuangshan, Yaguguan, Fushun, Fengji, Tongyuan, and other routes, to survey land and build fortresses and castles; to select generals and officials versed in frontier affairs to command at Kaiyuan—Xianzong approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Bing submitted a memorial asking for more troops in Liaoyang, forts built at key points from Fenghuangshan to Tongyuan, and seasoned frontier officers posted at Kaiyuan; Xianzong agreed to everything.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，朝鮮國王李瑈上言，遣中樞府知事康純等將兵征建州，渡鴨綠、潑猪<ref>疑同“婆猪江”</ref>二江，破兀獮府諸寨，擒李滿住及其子古納哈等，多所俘馘，使獻俘。

translations.literal: in the first month of the fourth year, Korean King Li Rui memorialized, dispatching the Secretariat director Kang Chun and others to lead troops against Jianzhou; they crossed the Yalu and Poju rivers, stormed the stockades of the Wunai district, captured Li Manzhu and his son Gunaha and others, took many captives and heads, and sent captives to present at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year King Li Rui of Korea reported that he had sent Kang Chun and other officials with an army against Jianzhou. They crossed the Yalu and Poju rivers, overran the Wunai stockades, seized Li Manzhu, Gunaha, and many others, and forwarded prisoners for presentation at court.

sentences.zh: 自阿哈出始領建州衞，傳其子釋加奴及孫李滿住。

translations.literal: from Ahaochu, who first held the Jianzhou Guard, it passed to his son Shijianu and grandson Li Manzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Ahaochu was the first to head the Jianzhou Guard; the line passed to his son Shijianu and then to his grandson Li Manzhu.

sentences.zh: 析左衛，猛哥帖木兒領之，死，而弟凡察代。

translations.literal: the left guard was split off; Mengge Temür led it; on his death his younger brother Fancha succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the left guard was carved out, Mengge Temür took command; after his death his younger brother Fancha replaced him.

sentences.zh: 既復傳其子董山；

translations.literal: it was then passed again to his son Dongshan;
translations.idiomatic: The post then passed to his son Dongshan.

sentences.zh: 析右衛，移凡察領之。

translations.literal: the right guard was split off, and Fancha was transferred to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: The right guard was split off and Fancha was moved to command it.

sentences.zh: 其入邊爲亂，董山爲之渠。

translations.literal: their raids across the border to make trouble—Dongshan was the ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: When they crossed the frontier to make war, Dongshan led them.

sentences.zh: 明既殺董山，朝鮮亦破李滿住，其子古納哈同死，他子都喜亦的哈，後不著。

translations.literal: once the Ming had killed Dongshan, Korea also defeated Li Manzhu; his son Gunaha died with him; another son, Duxiyedih, was later not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ming killed Dongshan, Korea crushed Li Manzhu; Gunaha died with his father, and another son, Duxiyedih, drops from the record thereafter.

sentences.zh: 凡察正統後不復見，當已前死。

translations.literal: Fancha was not seen again after the Zhengtong reign; he must already have died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Fancha never appears again after the Zhengtong era and had presumably died before then.

sentences.zh: 其子不花禿不與董山之亂，獨全。

translations.literal: his son Buhuatou did not join Dongshan's rebellion and alone survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: His son Buhuatou took no part in Dongshan's revolt and alone came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 他子阿哈答嘗朝於明，爭賜幣不及例。

translations.literal: another son, Ahada, once presented himself at the Ming court and disputed the gifts bestowed, not matching precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Another son, Ahada, once came to the Ming court and quarreled over his gifts, claiming they fell short of precedent.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，建州左衞都指揮佟那和劄等上章，爲董山子脫羅等、李古納哈子完者禿乞官。

translations.literal: in the sixth month of the fifth year, Jianzhou Left Guard regional commander Tongnaheza and others memorialized, pleading office on behalf of Dongshan's son Tuoluo and Li Gunaha's son Wanzhetu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year Tongnaheza, regional commander of the Jianzhou Left Guard, and others petitioned for offices for Tuoluo, son of Dongshan, and Wanzhetu, son of Li Gunaha.

sentences.zh: 兵部請進止，憲宗命授脫羅都指揮同知、完者禿都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: the Ministry of War requested instruction; Xianzong ordered Tuoluo appointed assistant regional commander and Wanzhetu regional vice-commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War asked for a decision; Xianzong appointed Tuoluo assistant regional commander and Wanzhetu regional vice-commander.

sentences.zh: 自是，凡從董山爲亂者，其子姓降一等，仍襲職。

translations.literal: from this time on, all who had followed Dongshan in rebellion—their descendants were demoted one grade yet still allowed to inherit office.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the descendants of everyone who had joined Dongshan's revolt were lowered one rank but still permitted to inherit their posts.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，建州三衞頭人沙加保等三百餘人朝於明，憲宗敕示威德，俾復奉朝貢。

translations.literal: in the first month of the sixth year, more than three hundred leaders of the three Jianzhou guards including Shajiabao presented themselves at the Ming court; Xianzong issued an edict displaying majesty and virtue, ordering them to resume tributary missions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year over three hundred Jianzhou leaders led by Shajiabao came to court; Xianzong's edict showed both power and mercy and bade them resume tribute.

sentences.zh: 居數年，太監汪直擅政，欲以邊功自重，巡撫遼東右副都御史陳鉞阿直意。

translations.literal: after several years, the eunuch Wang Zhi monopolized government, seeking to bolster himself with frontier achievements; Chen Yue, right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong, curried favor with Zhi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later the eunuch Wang Zhi dominated the government and sought to magnify himself with border victories; Chen Yue, grand coordinator of Liaodong, flattered his designs.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，上章言建州三衞爲邊患，請聲罪致討。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month of the thirteenth year, he memorialized that the three Jianzhou guards were a border menace and requested to proclaim guilt and launch a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he memorialized that the three Jianzhou guards were ravaging the frontier and asked leave to proclaim their crimes and attack.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，命兵部侍郎馬文升及鉞會議招撫，文升上言：「建州左、右二衞掌印都指揮脫羅、卜花禿等一百九十五人，建州衞掌印都指揮完者禿等二十七人，先后應命。

translations.literal: in the sixth month of the fourteenth year, Vice Minister of War Ma Wensheng and Yue were ordered to confer on appeasement and pacification; Wensheng memorialized: "The seal-holding regional commanders of the Jianzhou left and right guards—Tuoluo, Bohuatou, and others, 195 men; the seal-holding regional commander of the Jianzhou Guard—Wanzhetu and others, 27 men—have successively answered the summons."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year Ma Wensheng, vice minister of war, and Chen Yue were told to discuss pacification. Wensheng reported that 195 seal-holders of the left and right guards, including Tuoluo and Bohuatou, and 27 of the central guard, including Wanzhetu, had already come when summoned.

sentences.zh: 」宣敕撫慰，遺還。

translations.literal: an edict of consolation was proclaimed and they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of reassurance was read aloud and they were sent home.

sentences.zh: 卜花禿即不花禿，凡察子也。

translations.literal: Bohuatou is none other than Buhuatou; he was Fancha's son.
translations.idiomatic: The Bohuatou named in the memorial is Buhuatou, Fancha's son.

sentences.zh: 九年十二月、十一年正月，再入朝，至是同受招撫。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month of the ninth year and the first month of the eleventh year they again came to court; by then all alike received pacification.
translations.idiomatic: They had come to court again in the twelfth month of the ninth year and the first month of the eleventh; now at last they were all brought under the same pacification.

sentences.zh: 尋復命直詣遼東處置邊務，直至邊，鉞復請用兵。

translations.literal: soon after, Zhi was again ordered to go to Liaodong to manage frontier affairs; when he reached the border, Yue again requested use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was soon sent back to Liaodong to handle frontier affairs; once he arrived, Chen Yue again pressed for war.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月，命直監督軍務，撫寧侯朱永佩靖虜將印充總兵官，鉞參贊軍務，討建州三衞，並敕朝鮮國王李娎<ref>“娎”，折下女，讀xiào。

translations.literal: in the tenth month of the fifteenth year, Zhi was ordered to supervise military affairs; Zhu Yong, Marquis of Funing, wearing the Pacification-of-Barbarians general's seal as commander-in-chief, with Yue assisting military affairs, to campaign against the three Jianzhou guards; also ordering Korean King Li Xiao
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year Wang Zhi was put in charge of the campaign; Zhu Yong, Marquis of Funing, bore the Pacification-of-Barbarians seal as commander-in-chief with Chen Yue as his deputy, to strike the three Jianzhou guards; the court also ordered King Li Xiao of Korea

sentences.zh: </ref>發兵夾擊。

translations.literal: to send troops for a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: to march out and attack from the other side.

sentences.zh: 十一月，永等分道出撫順關，建州人拒守，縱擊破之，有所俘馘。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, Yong and others divided forces exiting Fushun Pass; Jianzhou people resisted and held; they were charged and broken; some captives and heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yong's columns issued from Fushun Pass; the Jianzhou tribesmen stood their ground but were overrun in a charge, with captives and heads taken.

sentences.zh: 師還，永等受上賞。

translations.literal: the army returned; Yong and others received lofty rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew and Yong and his colleagues were richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 十六年六月，建州復寇邊。

translations.literal: in the sixth month of the sixteenth year, Jianzhou again raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixteenth year Jianzhou raided the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 巡按遼東御史強珍疏論鉞等啟釁冒功，下吏議。

translations.literal: Qiang Zhen, investigating censor touring Liaodong, memorialized accusing Yue and others of provoking border troubles and claiming false merit; the case was referred to judicial officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor Qiang Zhen accused Chen Yue and his allies of provoking the border war and stealing credit; the matter was handed to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 汪直憾珍，劾珍欺罔，逮治，謫戍。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi resented Zhen, impeached Zhen for deception, had him arrested and tried, and banished him to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, nursing a grudge, impeached Zhen for fraud, had him arrested, and sent him into exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 鉞尋罷去。

translations.literal: Yue was soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue was soon removed from office.

sentences.zh: 十八年，直亦得罪，建州三衞奉朝貢如故。

translations.literal: in the eighteenth year, Zhi also fell from grace; the three Jianzhou guards presented tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Wang Zhi too was ruined, yet the three Jianzhou guards resumed tribute as of old.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，脫羅、完者禿皆進都督。

translations.literal: early in the Hongzhi reign, Tuoluo and Wanzhetu were both advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Hongzhi era both Tuoluo and Wanzhetu were promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 孝宗之世，脫羅三朝，完者禿五朝，明賜完者禿大帽、金帶。

translations.literal: in Xiaozong's reign, Tuoluo came to court three times, Wanzhetu five times; the Ming bestowed on Wanzhetu a grand cap and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaozong, Tuoluo presented himself at court three times and Wanzhetu five; the Ming gave Wanzhetu a state cap and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，脫羅卒，以其子脫原保襲都督僉事。

translations.literal: in the first year of Zhengde, Tuoluo died; his son Tuoyuanbao inherited the post of vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde Tuoluo died and his son Tuoyuanbao succeeded him as vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，卜花禿卒，賜祭。

translations.literal: in the fourth month of the second year, Bohuatou died; sacrificial gifts were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Bohuatou died and the court sent funeral offerings.

sentences.zh: 武宗之世，脫原保三朝。

translations.literal: in Wuzong's reign, Tuoyuanbao came to court three times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong, Tuoyuanbao came to court three times.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖閒，建州衞都督方巾，左衞都督章成、古魯哥，右衞都督阿剌哈、眞哥、騰力革輩，見於明實錄，皆不知其世。

translations.literal: during the Jiajing period, Jianzhou Guard regional commander Fangjin, Left Guard regional commanders Zhang Cheng and Guluge, Right Guard regional commanders Alaha, Zhenge, Tenglige, and their ilk appear in the Ming Veritable Records—all their generations are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era the Veritable Records mention regional commanders such as Fangjin of the central guard, Zhang Cheng and Guluge of the left, and Alaha, Zhenge, and Tenglige of the right—but their lineages are nowhere traced.

sentences.zh: 蓋自李滿住死，復傳其孫完者禿。

translations.literal: from Li Manzhu's death, succession passed again to his grandson Wanzhetu.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Manzhu's death the line evidently passed to his grandson Wanzhetu.

sentences.zh: 阿哈出之後，可紀者四世。

translations.literal: after Ahaochu, four generations are worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations after Ahaochu can be traced in the record.

sentences.zh: 其別子猛哥不花領毛憐衞，傳子撒滿哈失里<ref>“撒滿哈失里”，中華書局版此處作“撒滿答失里”，誤。

translations.literal: his son by another wife, Mengge Buhua, held the Maolian Guard and passed it to his son Samanhashili
translations.idiomatic: A son by another wife, Mengge Buhua, headed the Maolian Guard and passed it to Samanhashili

sentences.zh: </ref>，後不著。

translations.literal: ; later he is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: ; after that the line vanishes from the text.

sentences.zh: 董山死，傳其子脫羅及孫脫原保。

translations.literal: Dongshan died; it passed to his son Tuoluo and grandson Tuoyuanbao.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongshan died the post went to his son Tuoluo and then to his grandson Tuoyuanbao.

sentences.zh: 猛哥帖木兒之後，可紀者三世。

translations.literal: after Mengge Temür, three generations are worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations after Mengge Temür can be traced.

sentences.zh: 其弟凡察傳子不花禿，後不著。

translations.literal: his younger brother Fancha passed it to his son Buhuatou; later he is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Fancha, his younger brother, passed the line to Buhuatou, who then drops from the record.

sentences.zh: 迨嘉靖季年，王杲強，而阿哈出、猛哥帖木兒之族不復見。

translations.literal: by the closing years of Jiajing, Wang Gao grew powerful, while the clans of Ahaochu and Mengge Temür were no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Jiajing reign Wang Gao had grown formidable, and the houses of Ahaochu and Mengge Temür had disappeared from view.

sentences.zh: 王杲，不知其種族。

translations.literal: Wang Gao—his tribe is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Of Wang Gao's tribal origin nothing is known.

sentences.zh: 生而黠慧，通番、漢語言文字，尤精日者術。

translations.literal: from birth clever and sharp; versed in barbarian and Han languages and script; especially skilled in calendrical divination.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever from childhood, fluent in tribal tongues and written Chinese, and above all a master of calendrical arts.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，爲建州右衞都指揮使，屢盜邊。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign he became regional commander of the Jianzhou Right Guard and repeatedly raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era he held the post of regional commander of the Jianzhou Right Guard and raided the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 三十六年十月，窺撫順，殺守備彭文洙，遂益恣掠東州、會安、一堵牆諸堡無虛歲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirty-sixth year he spied on Fushun, killed garrison commander Peng Wenzhu, and thereafter grew ever bolder in plundering the forts of Dongzhou, Huian, and Yiduqiang—no year passed without incident.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of his thirty-sixth year he probed Fushun and killed Garrison Commander Peng Wenzhu; from then on he raided Dongzhou, Huian, Yiduqiang, and neighboring forts nearly every year.

sentences.zh: 四十一年五月，副總兵黑春帥師深入，王杲誘致春，設伏媳婦山，生得春，磔之，遂犯遼陽，劫孤山，略撫順、湯站，前後殺指揮王國柱、陳其孚、戴冕、王重爵、楊五美，把總溫欒、于欒、王守廉、田耕、劉一鳴等，凡數十輩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the forty-first year, vice regional commander Hei Chun led the army deep in; Wang Gao lured Chun in, set an ambush at Xifushan, captured Chun alive, and dismembered him; then he invaded Liaoyang, plundered Gushan, and raided Fushun and Tangzhan; before and after he killed commanders Wang Guozhu, Chen Qifu, Dai Mian, Wang Chongjue, and Yang Wumei and platoon leaders Wen Luan, Yu Luan, Wang Shoulian, Tian Geng, Liu Yiming, and others—several tens in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the forty-first year Vice Regional Commander Hei Chun marched deep into the hills; Wang Gao drew him in, ambushed him at Bride Hill, took him alive, and executed him by dismemberment. He then struck Liaoyang, looted Gushan, and overran Fushun and Tangzhan, killing Commanders Wang Guozhu, Chen Qifu, Dai Mian, Wang Chongjue, and Yang Wumei and Platoon Leaders Wen Luan, Yu Luan, Wang Shoulian, Tian Geng, Liu Yiming, and dozens besides.

sentences.zh: 當事議絕貢市，發兵剿，尋又請貸，杲不爲悛。

translations.literal: Those in charge discussed cutting off the tribute market, sent troops to suppress him, then again asked to show forbearance; Gao would not repent.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated ending the tribute trade and dispatching punitive columns, then wavered and pleaded for clemency—but Gao showed no remorse.

sentences.zh: 隆慶末，建州哈哈納等三十人款塞請降，邊吏納焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Longqing, thirty men of Jianzhou including Hahana and others came to the pass in submission seeking surrender; frontier officials accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Longqing reign thirty Jianzhou tribesmen led by Hahana presented themselves at the pass to surrender, and the border officials took them in.

sentences.zh: 王杲走開原索之，勿予，乃勒千餘騎犯清河。

translations.literal: Wang Gao ran to Kaiyuan to demand them; they were not given; then he mustered more than a thousand horsemen and invaded Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao rode to Kaiyuan to demand their return; when the garrison refused, he gathered a thousand horsemen and struck Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 游擊將軍曹簠伏道左，突起，斬五級，王杲遁走。

translations.literal: Mobile commander Cao Dai lay in ambush on the road's left, rose up suddenly, cut five heads, and Wang Gao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Commander Cao Dai lay in ambush beside the road, sprang up, and took five heads; Wang Gao fled.

sentences.zh: 故事，當開市，守備坐聽事，諸部酋長以次序立堂上，奉土產，乃驗馬；

translations.literal: By precedent, when the market opened the garrison commander sat in the audience hall; chieftains of the various tribes stood on the dais in order, presented native products, and only then were horses inspected;
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when the frontier market opened the garrison commander presided from the hall while chiefs of the various tribes lined the dais in turn, offered native goods, and only then submitted their horses for inspection;

sentences.zh: 馬即羸且跛，竝予善值，饜其欲乃已。

translations.literal: even if the horses were emaciated and lame, all were given a good price; only when their desires were sated would they stop.
translations.idiomatic: Even scrawny, lame beasts fetched top prices; the traders did not leave until every demand was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 王杲尤桀驁，攫酒飲，至醉，使酒箕踞罵坐。

translations.literal: Wang Gao was especially fierce and overbearing; he snatched wine and drank, until drunk commanding wine and sitting with legs sprawled, cursing those seated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao was the worst of them—seizing wine, drinking himself blind, then sprawling drunk upon the dais to revile the officials.

sentences.zh: 六年，守備賈汝翼初上，爲亢厲，抑諸酋長立階下，諸酋長爭非故事，盡階進一等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year garrison commander Jia Ruyi first took office; he was arrogant and harsh, pressing the chieftains to stand below the steps; the chieftains all disputed that this was not precedent and each advanced one step up.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the new garrison commander Jia Ruyi took a harsh line and forced the chiefs down to the steps; they protested that this broke custom and crowded one step higher.

sentences.zh: 汝翼怒，抵几叱之，視戲下箠不下者十餘人，驗馬必肥壯。

translations.literal: Ruyi grew angry, struck the table and shouted at them, regarded those who would not come down under the cudgel as more than ten men, and inspecting horses demanded they must be fat and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi slammed the table and berated them; more than a dozen who refused to descend he treated with contempt, and he would accept only fat, sturdy horses.

sentences.zh: 王杲鞅鞅引去，椎牛約諸部，殺掠塞上。

translations.literal: Wang Gao withdrew resentfully, slaughtered an ox to covenant with the tribes, and killed and plundered along the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao stalked off in a fury, sacrificed an ox to rally the tribes, and launched raids along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 是時，哈達王台方強，諸部奉約束，邊將檄使諭王杲。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Tai of Hada was just strong; the tribes all submitted to restraint; border generals dispatched envoys to instruct Wang Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai of Hada now held the tribes in check, and the border command sent envoys to warn Wang Gao.

sentences.zh: 王杲訟言汝翼摧抑狀，巡撫遼東都御史張學顏以聞，下兵部議，令遼東鎭撫宣諭，示以恩威。

translations.literal: Wang Gao pleaded the case of Ruyi's oppression; Zhang Xueyan, grand coordinator and censor-in-chief of Liaodong, reported it; it went down to the Ministry of War for deliberation, ordering Liaodong commander and grand coordinator to proclaim instruction, showing favor and awe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao petitioned over Ruyi's humiliations; Grand Coordinator Zhang Xueyan reported the affair to court; the Ministry of War ordered the Liaodong command to lecture him with both carrot and stick.

sentences.zh: 於是王台以千騎入建州寨，令王杲歸所掠人馬，盟於撫順關下而罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Tai with a thousand horsemen entered the Jianzhou stockade, ordered Wang Gao to return people and horses he had seized, and made alliance below Fushun Pass before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai then rode a thousand men into the Jianzhou camps, forced Wang Gao to return captives and livestock, and sealed the peace beneath Fushun Pass.

sentences.zh: 學顏復以聞，賚王台銀幣。

translations.literal: Xueyan again reported; Wang Tai was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan memorialized again and the court rewarded Wang Tai with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年七月，建州奈兒禿等四人款寨請降，來力紅追亡至塞上，守備裴承祖勿予，追者縱騎掠行夜者五人以去。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Wanli, four men of Jianzhou including Naierdu and others came to the stockade in submission seeking surrender; Lailihong pursued fugitives to the border; garrison commander Pei Chengzu did not grant them; the pursuers loosed horsemen and seized five travelers by night and took them away.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wanli 2 four Jianzhou men led by Naierdu asked to surrender at the stockade; Lailihong pursued fugitives to the border; Commander Pei Chengzu refused to hand them over, and the pursuers swept up five night travelers.

sentences.zh: 承祖檄召來力紅令還所掠，亦勿予。

translations.literal: Chengzu by dispatch summoned Lailihong ordering return of what was seized; again he did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu summoned Lailihong by dispatch to return the captives; again Pei refused.

sentences.zh: 是時王杲方入貢，馬二百匹、方物三十馱，休傳舍。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Gao was just presenting tribute—two hundred horses, thirty loads of regional products—resting at the relay hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao was then at court with tribute—two hundred horses and thirty loads of gifts—lodged at the courier station.

sentences.zh: 承祖度王杲必不能棄輜重而修怨於我，乃率三百騎走來力紅寨，諸部圍之，未敢動。

translations.literal: Chengzu judged that Wang Gao surely could not abandon heavy baggage and make enmity with us; then he led three hundred horsemen in a dash to Lailihong's stockade; the tribes surrounded them but did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Pei reckoned Wang Gao would not abandon his tribute train to feud with the Ming, led three hundred horse to Lailihong's camp, and found the tribes encircling him yet hesitant to strike.

sentences.zh: 王杲聞耗驚，馳歸，與來力紅入謁承祖，而諸部圍益眾。

translations.literal: Wang Gao hearing the news was alarmed, galloped back, and with Lailihong entered to pay respects to Chengzu, while the surrounding tribes grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by the news, Wang Gao galloped back with Lailihong to greet Pei, even as more tribes closed the ring.

sentences.zh: 王杲曰：「將軍幸毋畏，倉卒聞將軍至，皆匍匐願望見。

translations.literal: Wang Gao said: "General, pray do not fear; in haste hearing the general has come, all crawl prostrate wishing to look upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao said, "General, have no fear—these men heard you were coming and prostrated themselves in haste, eager only to see you.

sentences.zh: 」承祖知其詐，呼左右急兵之，擊殺數十人，諸部皆前鬭，殺傷相當。
