translations.literal: " Chengzu knew it was deception, called to his left and right to hurry troops upon them, struck and killed several tens; all the tribes came forward fighting; killings and wounds were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: Pei saw through the ruse, ordered his men to attack at once, and killed dozens; the tribes closed in and the casualties mounted on both sides.

sentences.zh: 來力紅執承祖及把總劉承奕、百戶劉仲文，殺之。

translations.literal: Lailihong seized Chengzu and platoon leader Liu Chengyi and company chief Liu Zhongwen, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Lailihong seized Pei, Platoon Leader Liu Chengyi, and Company Chief Liu Zhongwen, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 於是學顏奏絕王杲貢市。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xueyan memorialized to cut off Wang Gao's tribute market.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan then memorialized to terminate Wang Gao's tribute trade.

sentences.zh: 邊將復檄王台使捕王杲及來力紅。

translations.literal: Border generals again dispatched orders to Wang Tai to arrest Wang Gao and Lailihong.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier command again ordered Wang Tai to seize Wang Gao and Lailihong.

sentences.zh: 王台送王杲所掠塞上士卒，及其種人殺漢官者。

translations.literal: Wang Tai sent back soldiers on the border seized by Wang Gao, and his tribesmen who had killed Han officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai delivered soldiers Wang Gao had taken from the garrisons and tribesmen who had killed Ming officers.

sentences.zh: 王杲以貢市絕，部眾坐困，遂糾土默特、泰寧諸部，圖大舉犯遼、瀋。

translations.literal: Wang Gao because the tribute market was cut off, his tribes sat in distress; then he rallied Tümed, Taining, and other tribes, plotting a great thrust to invade Liaodong and Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from trade, Wang Gao's followers languished; he gathered the Tümed, Taining, and other tribes for a major strike at Liaodong and Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 總兵李成梁屯瀋陽分部諸將：楊騰駐鄧良屯，王維屏駐馬根單，曹簠馳大衝挑戰。

translations.literal: Regional commander Li Chengliang encamped at Shenyang and deployed his generals: Yang Teng garrisoned Dengliangtun, Wang Weiping garrisoned Magendan, Cao Dai galloped to Dachong to challenge battle.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Li Chengliang held Shenyang and fanned out his officers—Yang Teng at Dengliangtun, Wang Weiping at Magendan, Cao Dai riding to Dachong to offer battle.

sentences.zh: 王杲以諸部三千騎入五味子衝，明軍四面起，諸部兵悉走保王杲寨。

translations.literal: Wang Gao with three thousand horsemen of the tribes entered Wuzichenchong; Ming forces rose on four sides; tribal troops all ran to hold Wang Gao's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao led three thousand horse into Wuzichen Pass; Ming columns rose on every side and the tribes fell back to his stockade.

sentences.zh: 王杲寨阻險，城堅塹深，謂明軍不能攻。

translations.literal: Wang Gao's stockade was blocked and perilous, walls firm and moats deep; he deemed Ming forces could not attack.
translations.idiomatic: His fortress stood in rugged terrain behind stout walls and deep ditches, and he judged the Ming army could not take it.

sentences.zh: 成梁計諸部方聚處，可坐縛。

translations.literal: Chengliang calculated that where the tribes were just gathered, they could be bound sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang reckoned that with the tribes massed in one place he could take them without a prolonged siege.

sentences.zh: 十月，勒諸軍具礮石<ref>“礮”，同“砲”。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he compelled the armies to prepare cannon stones ["pao" is the same character as "cannon"].
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he ordered his troops to ready cannon stones

sentences.zh: </ref>、火器疾走圍王杲寨，斧其栅數重。

translations.literal: firearms, and with a rapid march surround Wang Gao's stockade, hacking through several layers of palisade.
translations.idiomatic: and firearms, rushed to encircle Wang Gao's stockade, and hewed through several rings of palisades.

sentences.zh: 王杲拒守，成梁益揮諸將冒矢石陷堅先登。

translations.literal: Wang Gao resisted defense; Chengliang yet more directed the generals to brave arrows and stones, storm the stronghold, and be first to scale.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao held out; Chengliang drove his generals through arrow and shot to breach the walls and lead the ascent.

sentences.zh: 王杲以三百人登臺射明軍，明軍縱火，屋廬、芻茭悉焚，烟蔽天，諸部大潰。

translations.literal: Wang Gao with three hundred men mounted a tower to shoot at Ming forces; Ming forces set fire; houses and fodder stacks were all burned, smoke obscuring heaven; the tribes greatly broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao manned a tower with three hundred archers; the Ming torched the houses and fodder stacks until smoke blotted the sky and the tribes broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 明軍縱擊，得一千一百四級。

translations.literal: Ming forces pursued the attack and took 1,104 heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming pressed the pursuit and claimed 1,104 enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 往時剖承祖腹及殺承奕者皆就馘，王杲遁走。

translations.literal: Those who in the past disemboweled Chengzu and killed Chengyi all had their heads taken; Wang Gao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had disemboweled Pei and slain Liu Chengyi were beheaded in turn; Wang Gao escaped.

sentences.zh: 明軍車騎六萬，殺掠人畜殆盡。

translations.literal: Ming army chariots and horse—sixty thousand—killed and plundered people and livestock nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty thousand Ming horse and cart swept the region, slaughtering men and beasts nearly to extinction.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，王杲復出，謀集餘眾犯邊，復爲明軍所圍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Wang Gao came out again, plotting to gather remnant forces and raid the border; again he was surrounded by Ming forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Wang Gao reappeared, mustering survivors for another border raid, only to be encircled again.

sentences.zh: 王杲以蟒褂、紅甲授所親阿哈納，陽爲王杲突圍走，明軍追之。

translations.literal: Wang Gao gave python robes and red armor to his intimate Ahana, feigning that it was Wang Gao breaking out and fleeing; Ming forces pursued.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed his trusted follower Ahana in his python robe and crimson armor, sent him out as a decoy, and the Ming gave chase.

sentences.zh: 王杲以故得脫，走重古路，將往依泰寧衞速把亥。

translations.literal: Wang Gao by this means got free, fled along Chonggulu, and was about to go rely on Subahei of Taining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he slipped free, fled toward Chonggulu, and meant to seek refuge with Subahei of the Taining Guard.

sentences.zh: 明軍購王杲急，王杲不敢北走，假道於王台。

translations.literal: Ming forces sought Wang Gao urgently with rewards; Wang Gao dared not flee north, and borrowed the road through Wang Tai.
translations.idiomatic: With the Ming offering a rich bounty, Wang Gao dared not flee north and instead begged passage through Wang Tai's territory.

sentences.zh: 邊吏檄捕送。

translations.literal: Border officials dispatched orders to seize and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier command issued orders for his capture and delivery.

sentences.zh: 七月，王台率子虎兒罕赤縛王杲以獻，檻車致闕下，磔於市。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wang Tai led his son Hutuerhanchi to bind Wang Gao and present him; he was sent in a caged cart to below the gates, and dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wang Tai and his son Hutuerhanchi bound Wang Gao and sent him in a prison cart to the capital, where he was executed by dismemberment in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 王杲嘗以日者術自推出亡不即死，竟不驗。

translations.literal: Wang Gao had once by calendrical arts deduced for himself that fleeing he would not immediately die; in the end it was not verified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao had once read the calendars and persuaded himself that flight would not bring swift death—the prophecy failed him.

sentences.zh: 妻孥二十七人爲王台所得，其子阿台脫去。

translations.literal: Wife and children—twenty-seven persons—were obtained by Wang Tai; his son Atai escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai took twenty-seven wives and children; only his son Atai got away.

sentences.zh: 阿台妻，清景祖女孫也。

translations.literal: Atai's wife was a granddaughter of the Qing Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Atai's wife was a granddaughter of the Qing founding lord Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 王台卒，阿台思報怨，因誘葉赫楊吉砮等侵虎兒罕赤。

translations.literal: Wang Tai died; Atai thought to repay the grudge, and thereby enticed Yang Jinu of Yehe and others to invade Hutuerhanchi.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Tai's death Atai sought revenge and incited Yang Jinu of Yehe and others to attack Hutuerhanchi.

sentences.zh: 總督吳兌遣守備霍九皋諭阿台，不聽。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Wu Dui sent garrison commander Huo Jiugao to instruct Atai; he would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wu Dui sent Commander Huo Jiugao to reason with Atai, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 李成梁率師禦之曹子谷、大梨樹佃，大破之，斬一千五百六十三級。

translations.literal: Li Chengliang led the army to meet them at Caozigu and Dalishutian, greatly defeated them, and cut 1,563 heads.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang met them at Caozigu and Dalishutian, shattered their force, and took 1,563 heads.

sentences.zh: 四年<ref>按阿台於萬曆四年尚依萬子虎兒罕，應不能擅出兵盜邊。

translations.literal: The fourth year [Note: Atai in the fourth year of Wanli still relied on Wanzi Hutuerhanchi; presumably he could not on his own send troops to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: "The fourth year" [Editorial note: In Wanli 4 Atai still depended on Hutuerhanchi and could hardly have raided on his own authority;

sentences.zh: 查勘其他文獻，此時應爲萬曆十一年。

translations.literal: Examining other documents, this time should be the eleventh year of Wanli.]
translations.idiomatic: cross-checking other sources shows the date should be Wanli 11.]

sentences.zh: </ref>春正月，阿台復盜邊，自靜遠堡九臺入，既又自榆林堡入至渾河，既又自長勇堡入薄渾河東岸，又糾土蠻謀分掠廣寧、開原、遼河。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring Atai again raided the border, entering from Jingyuan Fort's Jiutai, then again from Yulin Fort reaching Hun River, then again from Changyong Fort nearing the east bank of Hun River, and also rallied Tumen plotting to divide plunder among Guangning, Kaiyuan, and Liaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring Atai raided again—from Jiutai at Jingyuan Fort, then from Yulin Fort to the Hun River, then from Changyong Fort along the east bank of the Hun—and enlisted the Tumen for a split assault on Guangning, Kaiyuan, and the Liaoyang frontier.

sentences.zh: 阿台居古勒寨，其黨毛憐衞頭人阿海居莽子寨，兩寨相與爲犄角。

translations.literal: Atai dwelt at Gule stockade; his partisan Ah Hai, headman of Maolian Guard, dwelt at Mangzi stockade; the two stockades mutually formed a horn-and-corner defense.
translations.idiomatic: Atai held Gule Stockade while his ally Ah Hai of the Maolian Guard held Mangzi Stockade; the two camps supported each other like horns on a beast.

sentences.zh: 成梁使裨將胡鸞備河東，孫守廉備河西，親帥師自撫順王剛台出寨，攻古勒寨，寨陡峻，三面壁立，壕塹甚設。

translations.literal: Chengliang sent adjutant general Hu Luan to guard the east of the river, Sun Shoulian to guard the west of the river, and personally led the army from Fushun Wanggangtai out of the stockade to attack Gule stockade; the stockade was steep and precipitous, three sides cliff-like walls, moats and ditches very well set.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang posted Adjutant Hu Luan on the east bank of the river and Sun Shoulian on the west, then marched from Wanggangtai at Fushun to assault Gule Stockade—a fortress steep on three cliff faces with deep moats and ditches.

sentences.zh: 成梁麾諸軍火攻兩晝夜，射阿台，殪。

translations.literal: Chengliang directed the armies with fire attack for two days and nights, shot Atai, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang ordered two days and nights of fire assault, shot Atai, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 別將秦得倚已先破莽子寨，殺阿海，斬二千二百二十二級。

translations.literal: Separate commander Qin Deyi had already first broken Mangzi stockade, killed Ah Hai, and cut 2,222 heads.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Qin Deyi had already stormed Mangzi Stockade, killed Ah Hai, and taken 2,222 heads.

sentences.zh: 清景祖、顯祖皆及於難。

translations.literal: The Qing Jingzu and Xianzu both encountered the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Qing founding lords Jingzu and Xianzu were caught up in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 語詳太祖紀。

translations.literal: The account is detailed in the Annals of the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The full story is told in the Annals of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 同時又有王兀堂，亦不知其種族，所居寨距靉陽二百五十里，靉陽故通市。

translations.literal: At the same time there was also Wang Wutang; his tribe too is unknown; his dwelling stockade was two hundred fifty li from Aiyang; Aiyang formerly had market access.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there arose Wang Wutang—another man of unknown tribe whose stockade stood two hundred fifty li from Aiyang, a town that had long traded with the frontier.

sentences.zh: 王兀堂初起，奉約束惟謹。

translations.literal: Wang Wutang at first, submitting to restraint, was solely cautious.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Wutang kept the peace punctiliously.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，李成梁策徙孤山、險山諸堡，拓境數百里，斷諸部窺塞道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli Li Chengliang planned to move Gushan, Xianshan, and other forts, expanded territory several hundred li, and cut off the tribes' paths to spy on border routes.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 3 Li Chengliang relocated the Gushan and Xianshan garrisons, pushed the frontier forward by hundreds of li, and blocked the tribes' routes toward the passes.

sentences.zh: 王杲既擒，張學顏行邊，王兀堂率諸部酋環跪馬前，謂徙堡塞道，不便行獵，請得納質子，通市易鹽、布。

translations.literal: After Wang Gao was captured, Zhang Xueyan toured the border; Wang Wutang led the chieftains of the tribes in a ring kneeling before his horse, saying that moving the forts blocked border routes, was inconvenient for hunting, and requesting to be allowed to offer hostages and open markets to trade salt and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Gao's capture Zhang Xueyan toured the frontier; Wang Wutang and his chiefs knelt in a ring about his horse, protesting that the relocated forts blocked hunting routes and asking leave to send hostages and reopen trade in salt and cloth.

sentences.zh: 學顏以請，神宗許之。

translations.literal: Xueyan submitted the request; Shenzong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan memorialized the request and Shenzong approved.

sentences.zh: 開原、撫順、清河、靉陽、寬奠通布市自此始。

translations.literal: Cloth markets at Kaiyuan, Fushun, Qinghe, Aiyang, and Kuandian began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From that point cloth markets opened at Kaiyuan, Fushun, Qinghe, Aiyang, and Kuandian.

sentences.zh: 當是時，東方諸部落，自撫順、開原而北屬海西，王台制之；

translations.literal: At this time, eastern tribes from Fushun and Kaiyuan northward belonged to Haixi; Wang Tai controlled them;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eastern tribes from Fushun and Kaiyuan northward fell under Haixi and answered to Wang Tai;

sentences.zh: 自清河而南抵鴨綠江屬建州，王兀堂制之：頗守法。

translations.literal: from Qinghe south to the Yalu River belonged to Jianzhou; Wang Wutang controlled them: rather observant of law.
translations.idiomatic: from Qinghe south to the Yalu belonged to Jianzhou and to Wang Wutang, who for a time kept the peace.

sentences.zh: 已，漸竊掠東州、會安堡。

translations.literal: Later, he gradually stole and raided Dongzhou and Huian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he began raiding Dongzhou and Huian Fort.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，開市寬奠，參將徐國輔縱其弟若僕減直強鬻參，毆種人以回易至者幾斃，諸部皆忿，數掠寬奠、永奠、新奠諸堡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year the market opened at Kuandian; brigade commander Xu Guofu indulged his younger brother or servant to cut prices and forcibly sell ginseng, beat tribesmen who came to barter until nearly dead; all the tribes were angry and repeatedly raided Kuandian, Yongdian, and Xindian forts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year, when Kuandian market opened, Brigade Commander Xu Guofu let his brother or servant undersell ginseng by force and beat tribesmen who came to trade nearly to death; the tribes grew furious and raided Kuandian, Yongdian, and Xindian again and again.

sentences.zh: 他酋佟馬兒等牧松子嶺，闌入林剛谷。

translations.literal: Other chieftains Tong Ma'er and others pastured at Songziling, and trespassed into Linganggu.
translations.idiomatic: Other chiefs such as Tong Ma'er grazed at Songziling and strayed into Lingang Valley.

sentences.zh: 巡撫都御史周詠等劾國輔，罷之，諭王兀堂戢諸部。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator and censor-in-chief Zhou Yong and others impeached Guofu, dismissed him, and instructed Wang Wutang to restrain the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhou Yong impeached Guofu and removed him from office, then ordered Wang Wutang to rein in his tribes.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，王兀堂及他酋趙​​鎖羅骨等，以六百騎犯靉陽及黃關嶺，指揮王宗義戰死。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year Wang Wutang and other chieftains Zhao Suoluogu and others, with six hundred horsemen, invaded Aiyang and Huangguanling; commander Wang Zongyi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year Wang Wutang and chiefs including Zhao Suoluogu struck Aiyang and Huangguan Pass with six hundred horse; Commander Wang Zongyi fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 四月，又以千騎自永奠堡入，成梁帥師擊敗之，斬七百五十級，俘一百六十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, again with a thousand horsemen entering from Yongdian Fort, Chengliang led the army, defeated them, cut 750 heads, and captured 160 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month another thousand horse entered from Yongdian Fort; Chengliang routed them, took 750 heads, and captured 160 men.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復自寬奠堡入，副總兵姚大節帥師擊敗之，斬六十七級，俘十一人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, again entering from Kuandian Fort, vice regional commander Yao Dajie led the army, defeated them, cut 67 heads, and captured 11 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they entered again from Kuandian Fort; Vice Regional Commander Yao Dajie defeated them, took 67 heads, and captured 11 men.

sentences.zh: 王兀堂自是遂不振，不復通於明。

translations.literal: Wang Wutang from this time then did not revive, and no longer had contact with the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wang Wutang never recovered his strength and ceased all dealings with the Ming.

sentences.zh: 當隆慶之世，下逮萬曆初，建州諸衞以都督奉朝貢者，建州衞則有納答哈、納木章，左衞則有大疼克、八汗馬、哈塔台，右衞則有八當哈、來留住、松塔；

translations.literal: In the age of Longqing, down to early Wanli, among Jianzhou guards who as regional commanders presented court tribute: Jianzhou Guard had Nadaha, Namuzhang; Left Guard had Dategke, Bahamma, Hatatai; Right Guard had Badangha, Liuliuzhu, Songta;
translations.idiomatic: From the Longqing era into early Wanli, the Jianzhou guards who came to court as regional commanders included Nadaha and Namuzhang of the central guard, Dategke, Bahamma, and Hatatai of the left, and Badangha, Liuliuzhu, and Songta of the right;

sentences.zh: 而王杲自指揮使遷何秩，不可考見。

translations.literal: but from what rank Wang Gao was promoted from commandant, it cannot be examined and seen.
translations.idiomatic: but what office Wang Gao held before his promotion from commandant cannot be traced in the record.

sentences.zh: 王兀堂幷不著其官，然皆強盛爲大酋。

translations.literal: Wang Wutang moreover does not record his office, yet all were powerful and became great chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wutang's rank goes unrecorded, yet both men stood among the most powerful chiefs of their day.

sentences.zh: 自王杲就擒後五年而王兀堂敗，又後三年而阿台死，太祖兵起。

translations.literal: From Wang Gao's capture, five years later Wang Wutang was defeated; three years after that Atai died, and the Taizu's armies rose.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after Wang Gao's capture Wang Wutang fell; three years after Atai's death the Taizu took up arms.

sentences.zh: 論曰：建州之為衛始，自阿哈出枝幹互生，左右析置。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Jianzhou's becoming a guard began from Ahaochu, branches and stems mutually arising, left and right split and set apart.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The Jianzhou guards arose when Ahaochu's line divided into branches, the left and right guards being split off.

sentences.zh: 自永樂至嘉靖一百五十餘年，而阿哈出之世絕。

translations.literal: From Yongle to Jiajing, more than one hundred fifty years, and Ahaochu's generation ended.
translations.idiomatic: More than a century and a half passed from Yongle to Jiajing before Ahaochu's line died out.

sentences.zh: 王杲乘之起，父子弄兵十餘年乃滅。

translations.literal: Wang Gao seized the opportunity to rise; father and son played with arms more than ten years before perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao seized the moment to rise; father and son waged war for more than a decade before they were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其在於清，猶爽鳩、季荝之於齊，所謂因國是也。

translations.literal: His place in the Qing was like Shuangjiu and Jili in Qi—what is called inheriting a state is this.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing terms he played the part of Shuangjiu and Jili in Qi—the classic case of seizing upon an existing polity.

sentences.zh: 或謂猛哥帖木兒名近肇祖諱，子若孫亦相同。

translations.literal: Some say Mengge Temür's name neared the taboo name of the Founding Ancestor, and sons and grandsons were also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that Mengge Temür's name resembled the taboo of the Founding Ancestor and that his sons and grandsons bore the same likeness.

sentences.zh: 然清先代遘亂，幼子範察得脫，數傳至肇祖，始克復仇，而猛哥帖木兒乃被戕於野人，安所謂復仇？

translations.literal: Yet the Qing's early generations encountered disorder; the young son Fancha escaped; after several transmissions to the Founding Ancestor, only then could revenge be achieved—while Mengge Temür was killed by wild tribesmen; where is what is called revenge?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the early Qing house suffered calamity; the young son Fancha alone escaped; only after several generations did the Founding Ancestor exact revenge—whereas Mengge Temür was slain by wild tribesmen; what revenge is that?

sentences.zh: 若以範察當凡察，凡察又猛哥帖木兒親弟也，不得為數傳之祖。

translations.literal: If one takes Fancha to equal Fancha of the other reading, Fancha was again Mengge Temür's own younger brother and cannot be an ancestor of several transmissions.
translations.idiomatic: If one identifies Fancha with Fan Cha, Fan Cha was Mengge Temür's own younger brother and cannot stand as an ancestor several generations removed.

sentences.zh: 清自述其宗系，而明乃得之於簡書。

translations.literal: The Qing narrates its own clan lineage, while the Ming obtained it from brief records.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing tells its own genealogy; the Ming learned of it only from scattered documents.

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，名從主人，非得當時紀載如元秘史者，固未可以臆斷也。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals: names follow the host; without contemporary records such as the Yuan Secret History, one certainly cannot judge by speculation.
translations.idiomatic: As the Spring and Autumn tradition holds, names belong to their owners; without a contemporary record like the Yuan Secret History, speculation will not do.

sentences.zh: 隆慶、萬曆間，建州諸部長未有名近興祖諱者。

translations.literal: Between Longqing and Wanli, among Jianzhou tribal chiefs there was none whose name neared the taboo of the Rising Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing and Wanli reigns no Jianzhou chief bore a name resembling the taboo of the Rising Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵起，明人所論述但及景、顯二祖，亦未有謂為董山裔者。

translations.literal: When the Taizu's armies rose, what Ming people discussed and narrated reached only the Jing and Xian two ancestors; there was also none who said he was a descendant of Dongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu took up arms, Ming writers spoke only of the Jing and Xian ancestors; none called him a descendant of Dongshan.

sentences.zh: 信以傳信，疑以傳疑，今取太祖未起兵前建州三衛事可考見者著於篇，以阿哈出、王杲為之綱，而其子弟及同時並起者附焉。

translations.literal: What is credible transmit as credible, what is doubtful transmit as doubtful; now taking what can be examined and seen of the three Jianzhou guards before the Taizu raised armies, set it forth in this chapter, with Ahaochu and Wang Gao as its main threads, and their sons, brothers, and those who rose together at the same time appended.
translations.idiomatic: What is certain we record as certain, what is doubtful as doubtful; here we set down what can be verified of the three Jianzhou guards before the Taizu took up arms, with Ahaochu and Wang Gao as the main threads and their kin and contemporaries treated in turn.
